newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar committed to holding Mideast economic summit.
newsitem.headline: Qatar committed to holding Mideast economic summit.

text.p: Qatar is committed to holding a controversial Middle East-North Africa economic summit in November despite its inappropriate timing, Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani was quoted on Tuesday as saying.

"This summit is based on our conviction and we know that it is being organised at an inopportune time, but we are committed to this economic summit and it should go ahead," he said in an interview with the editors of Qatari newspapers.

Qatar, host of the conference, the fourth since landmark Middle East peace negotiations began in 1991, is under pressure from some Arab countries that oppose holding it because of the stalled peace process.
Israel attended the previous three summits.
Sheikh Hamad, who recently returned from a visit to the United States, postponing the summit if it failed to draw enough attendance. "I assure you, there will be no postponement...."

Asked if Israel would be invited, he said: "Israel has been invited to the previous summits in Arab countries...Be sure that if this were not so, there would no controversy and neither would it draw attention from the U.S. and other Western states."
Qatar had said Israel's attendance was contingent on progress in the peace process.
The president of Israel's Federation of Chambers of Commerce, Danny Gillerman, said on Sunday he was assured by Sheikh Hamad that Israel would be welcome.
He said he met Sheikh Hamad in New York last week along with senior U.S. and Arab officials at preparatory discussions on the economic summit.
